extracted.intended_audience: aircraft manufacturers/applicants for supplemental type certification, aircraft certification engineers, aviation safety regulators, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Special conditions and additional airworthiness safety standards the FAA requires for installation of rechargeable lithium batteries and battery systems on specified Gulfstream transport-category airplanes as part of the type-certification/supplemental type-certification basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain safe cell temperatures and pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: Be designed to maintain safe cell temperatures and pressures under all foreseeable operating conditions to prevent fire and explosion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Special Condition 1. Rationale: rechargeable lithium cells have different failure/operational characteristics than nickel-cadmium and lead-acid batteries; cells must be designed to avoid unsafe temperatures/pressures in all foreseeable conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent thermal propagation and control charge rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Be designed to prevent the occurrence of self-sustaining, uncontrollable increases in temperature or pressure, and automatically control the charge rate of each cell to protect against adverse operating conditions, such as cell imbalance, back charging, overcharging, and overheating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Special Condition 2. It addresses thermal runaway/propagation and requires automatic charge-rate control for each cell because lithium battery chemical reactions can act quickly; manual intervention would not be timely or effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: No emission of explosive or toxic gases
rubrics_metrics.description: Not emit explosive or toxic gases, either in normal operation or as a result of its failure, that may accumulate in hazardous quantities within the airplane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Special Condition 3. Batteries must not produce gases (normal or failure) that could accumulate to hazardous concentrations in airplane compartments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with flammable-fluid fire-protection (§25.863)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Special Condition 4. §25.863's flammable-fluid fire-protection requirements apply to rechargeable lithium battery installations because their electrolyte is a flammable fluid. Ensure areas exposed to flammable fluid leakage meet §25.863 protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent corrosive damage to adjacent structure and systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Not damage surrounding structure or adjacent systems, equipment, or electrical wiring from corrosive fluids or gases that may escape in such a way as to cause a major or more severe failure condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Special Condition 5. Focuses on preventing corrosive-fluid/gas escape from causing major-or-worse failure conditions to structure, systems, equipment, or wiring. Means of compliance may overlap with thermal-protection measures but address different hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent hazardous effects from maximum heat generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Have provisions to prevent any hazardous effect on airplane structure or systems caused by the maximum amount of heat it can generate due to any failure of it or its individual cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Special Condition 6. Addresses heat-generation hazards (distinct from corrosive-fluid hazards). Design must account for the maximum conceivable heat release from a cell or battery failure and protect structure/systems accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure sensing and flightcrew warning system
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a failure sensing and warning system to alert the flightcrew if its failure affects safe operation of the airplane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Special Condition 7. The battery/battery system must detect failures that could affect safe flight and provide a timely alert to the flightcrew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge-state monitoring and warning for safety-critical functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a monitoring and warning feature that alerts the flightcrew when its charge state falls below acceptable levels if its function is required for safe operation of the airplane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Special Condition 8. If the battery performs functions required for safe operation, there must be a monitoring/warning function to indicate low charge (below acceptable threshold).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic disconnect from charging source on failure/over-temperature
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a means to automatically disconnect from its charging source in the event of an over-temperature condition, cell failure or battery failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Special Condition 9. Requires automatic disconnect capability (not solely manual) to interrupt charging quickly in over-temperature, cell failure, or battery failure scenarios due to the fast-acting nature of lithium battery chemistry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Battery-system definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A battery system consists of the battery, battery charger and any protective, monitoring and alerting circuitry or hardware inside or outside of the battery. It also includes vents (where necessary) and packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note in the special conditions: for purposes of these requirements, 'battery' and 'battery system' are treated together; compliance and design considerations apply to the integrated system (battery, charger, protective/monitoring circuitry, vents, packaging).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special conditions substitute for existing battery regs when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: These special conditions apply to all rechargeable lithium batteries and battery system installations in lieu of §25.1353(b)(1) through (4) at amendment 25-123, or §25.1353(c)(1) through (4) at earlier amendments. Those regulations will remain in effect for other battery installations on these airplanes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these special conditions (rather than the cited §25.1353 subsections) for rechargeable lithium battery installations; retain existing regulations for non-lithium battery installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type certification basis and showing of continued compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 14 CFR 21.101, the applicant must show that the Gulfstream Model G-IV, GIV-X, GV, and GV-SP series airplanes, as changed, continue to meet the applicable provisions of the regulations listed in Type Certificate No. A12EA or the applicable regulations in effect on the date of application for the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicable airworthiness regulations do not contain adequate safety standards for a novel/unusual design feature, the FAA will prescribe special conditions under §21.16, and those special conditions become part of the type-certification basis under §21.101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and scope of special conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Special conditions are initially applicable to the model for which they are issued; if the applicant later applies for a supplemental type certificate to modify any other model included on the same type certificate to incorporate the same novel or unusual design feature, these special conditions would also apply to the other model under §21.101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These special conditions are not a rule of general applicability and affect only the applicant/applicable models, but they would also apply to any other model on the same type certificate modified to include the same novel design feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission guidance (most helpful comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most helpful comments reference a specific portion of the special conditions, explain the reason for any recommended change, and include supporting data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting comments (by regulations.gov, mail, hand delivery, or fax), identify the docket number, reference specific text, provide reasons for suggested changes, and include data to support recommendations; the FAA will consider comments and may change special conditions based on received comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) designation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If comments contain commercial or financial information that is customarily and actually treated as private, clearly designate the submitted comments as CBI by marking each page containing CBI as 'PROPIN' and send such submissions to the identified FAA contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBI will be treated confidentially under FOIA and will not be placed in the public docket; comments not so designated will be placed in the public docket and posted to regulations.gov. Follow the For Further Information Contact instructions for sending CBI.
